notes:
Shorthand CRM notes and call excerpts:
- Customer: mid-market SaaS for B2B support automation (multi-tenant product support chat + agent assist).
- Why evaluating: saw consistent latency regressions from incumbent since Dec (higher first-byte times, token jitter). UX complaints (agents and end-users).
- Primary ask: Hosted API that can meet streaming SLOs (1st-byte <150ms median, per-token <60ms median) and smooth tool-calling/func-calls with low jitter; then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput once SLA validated.
- POC scope: shadow 10% of traffic for 3 days, exact same prompts and tool-calls, capture token-level latencies and failure modes. Redwood running streaming path + prefix caching; incumbent using their streaming blocks.
- Initial bench summary (03/03): Redwood hosted streaming median 1st-byte 90ms, per-token 40ms; incumbent median 1st-byte 320ms, per-token 120ms. Tail (95th): Redwood ~260ms, incumbent ~1.1s.
- Customer quote: "We started seeing regressions after vendor rolled model changes in Dec — response times spiked and streaming became choppy. If you can keep <200ms tail we win a huge UX uplift."
- Observability asks: token-level traces, per-route cost breakdowns, ability to pin model version and automatic fallback to cheaper variant on overload.
- Pricing: procurement wants committed Dedicated pricing vs pay-as-you-go; looking at $10k-$25k/mo band depending on committed qps + burst. Need Redwood to provide clear cost delta vs incumbent including caching savings.
- Compliance: must support SSO (SAML), KMS for encryption-at-rest, audit logs retention 1 year, and EU data residency for some customers (multi-region).
- Next: SE to run 3-day POC (start 2026-03-08), deliver benchmark spreadsheet and a sample SLO report; AE to get preliminary Dedicated pricing table by 2026-03-10. Legal to start residency/KMS paperwork (eta 2 weeks).
- Risks: procurement inertia; incumbent offering retroactive credits to retain; deeper legal requirements for some EU customers could push to Private.
- Internal notes: follow up with benchmarks broken down by prompt length/avg tokens and by function-calls vs plain generation. Capture jitter and spike scenarios.
